to occur. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=52}} {{GHGheb|text=אַֽחֲיוֹתֵךְ}} occurs (for {{GHGheb|text=אַחְיֹתַ֫יִךְ}}). In the forms {{GHGheb|text=אֲחוֹתַי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=13}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲחוֹתַ֫יִךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=51.55.61}} (to be read also in verse 45 for {{GHGheb|text=אֲחוֹתֵךְ}}, which has been erroneously assimilated to the singular occurring in vv. 48, 49, 56), and {{GHGheb|text=אֲחֽוֹתֵיכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=2|verse=3}} (for which, however, read {{GHGheb|text=אֲחֽוֹתְכֶם}}), the third radical has been entirely lost.

{{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ|translate=man}}, according to the common opinion either incorrectly lengthened for {{GHGheb|text=אֵשׁ}} (from ''ʾišš'', with assimilation of the ''Nûn'' of the ground-form ''ʾinš'', which again has been attenuated from ''ʾanš'' from the stem {{GHGheb|text=אָנַשׁ}}), or softened directly from ''ʾinš''. It is, however, probable that a separate stem ({{GHGheb|text=אישׁ|translate=to be strong}}?) is to be assumed for the singular<ref>So already Gesenius in his {{GHGcite|title=Thes. linguae Hebr.}}, i. 83 f., and recently again Friedr. Delitzsch, ''Prolegg.'', p. 160 ff., Praetorius in Kuhn’s ''Orient. L.-B.'', 1884, p. 196; König, ''Lehrgeb''., ii. 38; while Nöldeke ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1886, p. 739 f.), against Delitzsch, would connect both {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}} and {{GHGheb|text=נָשִׁים}} with the stem {{GHGheb|text=אנשׁ}}.</ref>; consequently the stem {{GHGheb|text=אָנַשׁ|translate=to be sociable}}, <section end=par96 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
